original_question: A previously healthy 36-year-old man comes to the physician for a yellow discoloration of his skin and dark-colored urine for 2 weeks. He does not drink any alcohol. Physical examination shows jaundice. Abdominal and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. Serum studies show increased levels of alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST). A liver biopsy is performed and a photomicrograph after periodic acid-Schiff-staining is shown. Which of the following is the most likely additional finding in this patient?

base.stage_1: A 36-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of yellow discoloration of his skin and dark urine for the past two weeks.
base.stage_2: The patient's physical exam reveals jaundice. Abdominal and neurological exams are unremarkable. Vital signs are within normal limits.
base.stage_3: Laboratory studies reveal elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. A liver biopsy was performed showing PAS-positive globules.
base.stage_4: A chest CT reveals bullous changes at the lung bases.

counterfactuals.alteration_description: The patient's physical exam reveals jaundice and mild splenomegaly, which argues against alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency as it is not typically associated with splenomegaly.
counterfactuals.stage_1: A 36-year-old man presents to the clinic complaining of yellow discoloration of his skin and dark urine for the past two weeks.
counterfactuals.stage_2: The patient's physical exam reveals jaundice. Palpation of the abdomen reveals mild splenomegaly. Neurological exam is unremarkable. Vital signs are within normal limits.
counterfactuals.stage_3: Laboratory studies reveal elevated alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels. A liver biopsy was performed showing PAS-positive globules.
counterfactuals.stage_4: A chest CT reveals bullous changes at the lung bases.
